title: A December invoice is due in January of the next year
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • Scenario: A customer on the shop's own term due on the 10th of the following month is invoiced in December.
  • You are an Admin user working at {Location-A}.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • Customer {Customer-A} holds the shop's own term {Term-A}, due on day 10 of the following month.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-07 Customer and {Term-A} is ZZAUTOTEST DATA-07 Tenth.
  • Work order {Work-order-1} for {Customer-A} is complete and ready to invoice (every part received, review done).
    For example: {Work-order-1} is S2-15440.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open {Work-order-1}'s Finance tab.
  2. Set Invoice Date to Dec 15, 2026.
  3. Set Invoice Date to Dec 31, 2026.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the invoice preview shows Invoice Date and Due date.
  • Step 2: the Due date reads Jan 10, 2027 (the month after December is January of the next year).
  • Step 3: the Due date reads Jan 10, 2027.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R4: “An invoice dated in December on a "day of the following month" term is due in January of the next year (day 10, invoice Dec 15 2026, due Jan 10 2027).”
